title: Nothing a request can send terminates or wedges a worker
scope:
decides what happens on the failure paths that reach a worker *around* the mechanisms already
in place — a process `abort()`, a `SIGSEGV` raised by the engine's own recursion, a `SIGBUS` from a file
that moved under a mapping, an accept loop that spins, a core that is alive but never returns. Decides the
admission arithmetic that makes a memory cap mean something, and names the one fault class that survives
all of it. Does **not** re-decide how a `FATAL` is reported once it reaches a boundary
([0020](0020.md)), which text a parser refuses
([0095](0095.md)), what a proxy owns
([0074](0074.md)), or the regex engine's own bound
([0056](0056.md)).
dependsOnText:
[0002](0002.md) — this ADR extends its containment rule outward and has
nothing to decide without it.

summary.headline: Nothing a request can send kills or wedges a worker
summary.body:
Catching a panic contains a panic, but not a process abort, not a signal, and not a worker that
stays alive without making progress — so containment covers the whole worker task, and every
depth and duration a request can drive is bounded inside the engine. A worker never blocks on a
system call; one that stops progressing is shed by its deadline, not killed; and admission is
arithmetic against the memory budget. One fault class remains — a memory bug in unsafe code or a
miscompile — and it is named, not hidden.
